amendments.rule: A construct noun cannot take the article, so a pointed `בַּ` before one is preposition-only and the English *the* is supplied. Follow MACULA's morphology rather than the pointing. Where the chain's *nomen rectum* does carry an article, that morpheme takes the *the* the ASV writes for the chain even though English fronts it to the phrase's left edge and renders the rectum anarthrously — `לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים` → *the two tables of stone*, `כּוּר הַבַּרְזֶל` → *the furnace of iron*. Supply a *the* on a construct noun only where no article morpheme is present, or for a second English *the* in a multi-level chain, which the article's own leaves for the outer construct: `לְבַב כָּל בְּנֵי הָאָדָם` → *the hearts of all the children of men*. **Fronting is what the anarthrous rendering forces, not a preference for the phrase's left edge.** Where the ASV instead renders the rectum arthrously, writing a *the* before the construct and another before the rectum — `מִשְׁפַּחַת הַקְּהָתִי` → *the families of the Kohathites*, `בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי` → *the sons of the Kohathites*, `שְׂדֵה הָעִיר` → *the fields of the city*, `מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַלֵּוִי` → *the families of the Levites* — nothing is fronted: the article takes the *the* standing before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one, exactly as an outer construct does in a multi-level chain. Count the ASV's *the*s and read which word each stands before, as rule 47 reads which word its single *the* stands before. **A construct relation the ASV recasts as an English possessive is not a fronting either.** Where the ASV writes the rectum as a possessive standing before its head noun — `מִלַּת מַלְכָּא` → *the king's matter*, `שַׁלִּיטָא דִּי מַלְכָּא` → *the king's captain*, `שַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ` → *the king's gate* — the *the* at the phrase's left edge stands before the possessor's own word, because an English possessive expression takes the determiner of the possessor and not of the head noun. So the article on the rectum takes it and the construct noun keeps only its own word, a present article morpheme taking its English before a supplied one does; supply a *the* on the construct only where the ASV writes a second one, as `רַב טַבָּחַיָּא דִּי מַלְכָּא` → *the captain of the king's guard* does. Do not read the left edge as evidence of fronting: what fronting answers to is an anarthrous rectum, and here the rectum is the very word the *the* determines. A `דִּי` or other relational morpheme standing between the two nouns is rendered inside the possessive and shares the rectum's unit under rule 30. **A rectum that is a proper name is not an exception.** An article MACULA segments off a toponym takes the ASV's *the* on the same terms as one on a common noun, and is never set aside as lexicalized in the name: `בְּנֵי הָרָמָה` → *The children of Ramah* and `אַנְשֵׁי בֵית אֵל וְהָעָי` → *The men of Beth el and Ai* give the single written *the* to the article and leave the construct noun bare. **But an article the ASV spells into its name is already rendered.** Where the rectum is transliterated with its article — `בְּנֵי הַסֹּפֶרֶת` → *the children of Hassophereth* — the article shares the name's unit under rule 30, it has taken its *the* inside that English word rather than as a separate one, and the *the* the ASV does write stands before the construct as a supplied one. Read the transliteration before counting: nothing is fronted from an article English has already spelled out. Mark the article `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all, as in `הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה` → *these cities*.
amendments.why: Rule 29's fronting sentence covers an anarthrous *of*-rendering of the rectum and says nothing about the ASV's other common recasting, the English possessive, where the single *the* also stands at the phrase's left edge. Two DAN.2 verse passes read that left edge as fronting and gave the *the* to the construct (2.10, 2.23), while two others read which word it stands before and gave it to the article on the rectum (2.14, 2.15) — the same phrase, *the king's matter* and *the king's captain*, analysed two ways inside one chapter. English syntax settles it: in *the king's matter* the determiner belongs to the possessor NP, so rule 29's own counting instruction, and rule 47's principle that a present article morpheme takes its English before a supplied one does, both put it on the rectum's article. The corpus corroborates: of 820 `מֶלֶךְ` units it records 42 holding a bare *king's* against 2 holding *the king's*, so the determiner is normally aligned outside the possessor noun's own unit. The added sentences also state the Aramaic case explicitly, since rule 15 already treats a separately segmented determined-state ending as an article, and name the `דִּי` that stands inside such a possessive so that a later pass does not split it out.

conventions: Aramaic possessive recasting of a construct chain: where the ASV writes the rectum as an English possessive (millat malka -> 'the king's matter', shallita di malka -> 'the king's captain', rab tabbahayya di malka -> 'the captain of the king's guard'), the phrase's one written 'the' stands before the possessor and belongs to the determined-state ending on that noun; the construct noun keeps only its own word, and takes a supplied 'the' only where a second one is written. 2.10 and 2.23 were corrected to this, which 2.14 and 2.15 already had.

kol-qobel (di / dnah): where the ASV renders the whole expression by one indivisible connective - 'because' (2.8), 'forasmuch as' (2.10, 2.40, 2.41, 2.45), 'Therefore' (2.24) - it is one noncompositional unit headed on qobel and on the English anchor. Where the ASV instead spends a word on dnah itself, that morpheme is its own unit and the remaining kol-qobel is an ordinary aligned unit: 2.12 'For this cause' gives 'this' to dnah and 'For ... cause' to kol-qobel.

Fusion status in this chapter: a rule-30 fusion is recorded aligned unless corpus precedent for that particular expression is uniformly noncompositional. Noncompositional here: kol-qobel di, mah di -> 'what', ke di -> 'as', ki dnah -> 'such', di + suffix -> 'whose', di + le + suffix -> 'unto whom', ahare dnah -> 'hereafter', ka hadah -> 'together', le + suffix -> 'his'. Aligned here: be-edayin -> 'Then', la + bi -> 'without', min qodam, lipne, ad di, al mah, le-qobel, min qesat, be-kol di, hazeh hawayta. The corpus is itself divided on fusion status generally (lipne -> 'before' is 230 noncompositional to 201 aligned), so this is a chapter convention, not a contract rule.

Haphel yeda (and hawi) with a pronominal object suffix: where the ASV writes 'make known unto/to X', the supplied preposition belongs to the verb's unit under rule 44, and the suffix takes only its pronoun. 2.5 and 2.9 were corrected to this, which 2.23 (twice), 2.26 and 2.29 already had, and which is how the corpus reads DAN.5.15, 5.16 and 5.17.

report: Four real cross-verse splits; ten verses patched. No BSB comparison or validation report was included in this packet, so there is nothing on that head to adjudicate; say so rather than assume there were none.

Split 1 (construction, not style): 'the king's matter' at 2.10 and 2.23 gave the phrase's one written 'the' to the construct noun (millat) and marked the determined-state ending on malka unrepresented, while 2.14 and 2.15 gave that 'the' to the ending on malka and left the construct with only its own word. Rule 29 says count the ASV's 'the's and read which word each stands before, and in an English possessive the left-edge determiner stands before the possessor ('the king' + 's), not before the head noun. 2.14 and 2.15 are right; 2.10 and 2.23 are corrected. This is the amendment to rule 29 below.

Split 2: Haphel yeda with an object suffix rendered 'make known unto X'. 2.5 and 2.9 put the supplied 'unto' on the suffix; 2.23 (twice), 2.26 and 2.29 put it on the verb. Rule 44's supplied-preposition clause governs a bare object with no preposition of its own, and the corpus reads it that way (DAN.5.15 'make known unto', DAN.5.16 and 5.17 'make known to', all headed on 'known'). 2.5 and 2.9 corrected; the suffix keeps only its pronoun.

Split 3: kol-qobel (di) rendered by one indivisible connective was noncompositional at 2.10 and 2.45 but aligned at 2.8, 2.40 and 2.41 - at 2.40/2.41 against 2.45 the English is the identical 'forasmuch as'. Corpus precedent for this expression is unanimous: seven noncompositional units at DAN.3.29, 4.18, 5.12, 5.22, 6.10 and elsewhere, and no aligned one. 2.8, 2.24, 2.40 and 2.41 move to noncompositional. 2.12 is left aligned and split from dnah, because there the ASV writes 'this' for dnah and 'For ... cause' for the rest, so the expression as a whole is not one indivisible connective.

Split 4: two status splits on identical expressions - be-edayin -> 'Then' (aligned 2.14, 2.46; noncompositional 2.35) and la + bi -> 'without' (aligned 2.34; noncompositional 2.45). The corpus rules on neither, and is itself divided on fusion status generally (lipne -> 'before' is 230 noncompositional against 201 aligned). I harmonised to the chapter's dominant treatment of two-morpheme fusions, which is aligned (min-qodam three times, lipne, ad di, al mah, le-qobel, min qesat, be-kol di), and for the negative fusion to the nearest corpus analogue, where waw plus lo is 163 aligned to 67 noncompositional for 'nor' and 128 to 122 for 'neither'. 2.35 and 2.45 corrected; 2.14, 2.34 and 2.46 stand.

One partition defect fixed in passing: DAN.2.10 assigned target t019 ('show') twice, to the lamed and to the infinitive. Rule 52 puts nothing on a preposition for which the ASV writes no word, so the lamed is now unrepresented and the infinitive holds t019.

Checked and found source-licensed, not splits: the determined-state ending aligned or unrepresented by whether the ASV writes a 'the'; min rendered 'part' with 'of' going to a following di where one stands (2.33, 2.41) and 'part of' where none does (2.41, 2.42); the 3fp suffixes of minnehen unrepresented throughout (2.33, 2.41, 2.42), since the ASV writes no 'of them'; supplied 'as for' marked added at 2.29, 2.30 and 2.32 alike, no marker standing on the fronted phrase; kol as 'any', 'all', 'whole' or unrepresented with the negative taking the recast determiner at 2.10 and 2.35; the vocative article unrepresented at 2.4, 2.29, 2.31, 2.37; hakkime heading on 'wise' in all nine units; hoda heading on 'known' and shelet on 'rule' throughout.
